_comment: Friendly names for `python atlas.py get <name>`. Each entry names a NIST
Public Data Repository record and, optionally, a default --filter so a
first run pulls a small slice rather than the whole record.
Add your own: any record id, ark, DOI or landing URL works here, and
atlas.py works without this file at all if you pass the id directly.
sample: how many of the smallest files 'a sample' means in the menu.
reads: which reader handles the record's files.
Only records ATLAS can actually ingest are listed. Other public NIST I/Q
records exist but ship formats nothing here reads yet (HDF5, zipped CSV,
MATLAB); they are catalogued in docs/README_MANUAL.md instead of here, so
nothing in this menu downloads gigabytes it cannot then draw.

lte-uplink.title: High-SNR I/Q Recordings of FDD LTE User Equipment Emissions
lte-uplink.note: 902 files / 188 GB. The default filter takes the 1.4MHz set, whose captures are ~37 MB each. Pass --filter '' for the whole record.

tig-welding.title: Electromagnetic Interference Measurements from Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) Arc Welding
tig-welding.note: Same iq-tar layout as microwave-oven. Arc-welding emissions at 900 MHz, 2.4 GHz and 5.3 GHz; 625 MS/s, 160 MHz span, ~400 MB per capture. 352 files / 16 GB in total.

cbrs-sea.title: SEA-DATA Web Portal (NASCTN CBRS SEA monitoring)
cbrs-sea.note: The record is access instructions rather than the data: it points at github.com/usnistgov/SEA-DATA and a NIST Box share you request from nasctn@nist.gov. Once the CSV exports are on disk, `atlas.py get <folder>` ingests them. Documented in NIST TN 2359. Supersedes mds2-4214, which was never published and returns HTTP 404.
